cases.description: After PipeWriter.CloseWithError(first), a second CloseWithError(second) returns nil without replacing the first error; a later reader receives first.
If a six-byte Pipe write has delivered two bytes and the reader closes with an error, the writer returns the two consumed bytes together with that error.
A zero-length Pipe write still participates in a reader handshake; after a matching zero-length Read both return zero and nil.

With strings.NewReader("x") and no prior non-EOF reader error, a split function returning ErrFinalToken with a non-nil empty token makes Scan return true once, then false with nil Err; with a nil token the first Scan is false with nil Err.
Calling Scanner.Buffer or Scanner.Split after Scan was called panics even when the first Scan returned false for empty input.
atomic.Value.Store accepts a typed nil pointer as a non-nil interface; Store(nil) panics, and the existing typed value remains.

On an empty atomic.Value, CompareAndSwap with non-nil old and new values of the same concrete string type returns false and leaves it empty; CompareAndSwap(nil, a non-nil string) initializes it and returns true.
